title: Can You Change Schools Mid-Course?
summary: Legally the transfer is a notification, not a permission. The deadline everyone watches is 14 days. The one that ends residence status is three months.
body_html:
Changing schools is usually discussed as though immigration has to approve it. It does not. The transfer is a notification you file, not a permission you request.

That sounds reassuring, and it is — right up to the part where the real risk lives somewhere else entirely.

Transfer is a notification, and it is two of them

Where your activity organisation changes its name or address, ceases to exist, where you leave it, or where you transfer to another one, you must notify the Commissioner of the Immigration Services Agency within 14 days. [source:1] The authority is Article 19-16, item 1 of the Immigration Control Act. [source:1]

The agency defines both terms, and the definitions are the part worth reading.

Leaving means you have finished your activity at the organisation — through changing jobs, resigning, or graduating. [source:1] Transferring means you have come to belong to a new organisation, through changing jobs or advancing in study. [source:1]

So a school change is both events: you leave one organisation and you join another. The agency keeps separate notification forms for each, and provides a third form for filing both at the same time. [source:1]

This is where people file half of what they owe. Students who quit and enrol elsewhere often report only the new school — the joining — and never report the leaving. Both are listed, and the combined form exists precisely because the two normally happen together. [source:1]

The deadline that actually ends your status

The 14 days above is the notification deadline. [source:1] Missing it is a separate problem. It is not the number that decides whether you keep your residence status.

That number is three months.

Residence status may be revoked where a person holding a status listed in the upper column of Appended Table I has not carried out the activity for that status continuously for 3 months or more, unless there is a legitimate reason for not doing so. [source:2] This is ground (6) under Article 22-4, paragraph 1. [source:2] Student status is in that table. [source:2]

Now put the two together. The gap between leaving one school and starting at the next is time during which you are not carrying out your status activity. Nobody schedules a three-month gap deliberately. They get one anyway — the new school's next intake is in April, it is now January, and the old school has already removed them from its register.

There is a separate and faster ground. Where a person is not carrying out the activity for their status and is carrying out, or intends to carry out, another activity instead, that is ground (5), with no three-month wait attached. [source:2] And where there is reasonable cause to suspect the person would flee, ground (5) leads directly to deportation procedures rather than to a departure period. [source:2]

The practical reading: a gap in which you are studying nothing is measured in months. A gap in which you are working instead is not.

"Legitimate reason" is real, and it is not a form

Both grounds carry the same exception — unless there is a legitimate reason for not carrying out the activity. [source:2] That exception is doing a lot of work in these provisions, and it is worth being honest about what it is.

It is not a category you apply for. The agency states that whether a revocation ground applies is judged according to the specific circumstances of each case, and that even where a ground does apply, whether revocation actually happens is decided in light of how it came about and the person's subsequent situation of residence. [source:2]

So a documented reason helps and a plausible story does not. The difference between the two is paper you can produce: an admission letter with a start date, correspondence with both schools, a medical certificate.

If it does go wrong, there is a hearing

Revocation is not a letter that arrives one morning. An immigration inspector is required to hear the opinion of the foreign national concerned, and that person may state an opinion, submit evidence, and request inspection of the materials. [source:2]

Outcomes differ by ground. Where grounds (3) through (10) apply, a period for departure is designated, up to a maximum of 30 days, and the person leaves voluntarily within it. [source:2] Where grounds (1) or (2) apply — obtaining permission through deceit — the person is immediately subject to deportation procedures. [source:2] Failing to leave within the designated period means deportation and criminal penalty. [source:2]

A transfer gap falls in the ground (5) and ground (6) range. [source:2] That is the difference between a bad situation and an unrecoverable one, and it is worth knowing which one you are in.

It comes back at renewal

Suppose you keep your status through the transfer. The gap is still on your record, and renewal is where it surfaces.

The agency's guideline on changes of status and renewals evaluates as a negative factor a student who continued residing in Japan after being removed from the register or withdrawing, unless there is a legitimate reason for not carrying out the activity. [source:3]

Note the wording: removed from the register or withdrawing. A clean voluntary withdrawal to transfer is covered by the same sentence as being expelled. What saves it is the legitimate reason, which is the same standard as above and the same requirement to be able to show something.

And the guideline says plainly that even where every consideration is satisfied, permission may still not be granted once all circumstances are weighed together. [source:3] There is no version of this where the transfer is guaranteed to be invisible.

How to file, and one difference worth noticing

Three routes are available. [source:1]

Online, the electronic notification system runs 24 hours, 365 days, shows the history and processing status of what you have filed — and requires no supporting documents to be submitted. [source:1] First-time users register before filing. [source:1]

At a counter, present your residence card and submit the notification form. [source:1]

By post, enclose the form and a copy of your residence card, and mark the envelope in red with 届出書在中 or NOTIFICATION ENCLOSED. [source:1] The agency does not acknowledge receipt of postal notifications and recommends a delivery method that leaves a tracking record. [source:1]

That last point is worth sitting with. For an obligation with a deadline and no acknowledgement, the only proof you filed is the proof you created yourself. Online is the route that gives you a status record. [source:1]

Incidentally, post is accepted here and is not accepted for a certificate of eligibility application. [source:1] The routes differ by procedure, so do not carry an assumption across from one to the other.

The order that avoids all of this

  • Secure written admission from the new school, with a start date, before you leave the old one. The gap is created by the order you do things in.
  • Ask the old school when it will remove you from its register. That date, not the date you stopped attending, is the one that matters on paper.
  • File both notifications — the leaving and the joining — within 14 days of the events. [source:1] Use the combined form if they coincide. [source:1]
  • If a gap is unavoidable, document why before it starts, not afterwards.
  • Do not take up other work to fill the gap. That moves you from the three-month ground to the one without a waiting period. [source:2]
  • Keep the admission letter and both filing records until your next renewal is granted, because that is when they get asked about. [source:3]

One thing this article cannot tell you: whether the new school will take you mid-course. That is the school's decision, it depends on whether a class at your level has a place, and it is unrelated to the immigration question. Our role is to prepare and forward documents — the school decides admission, the agency decides status, and tuition is paid directly to the school.

Related: what happens if you stop attending and do not transfer at all, in stopping attendance and withdrawal; the full list of considerations at renewal in what renewal actually assesses; the other reporting duties and their deadlines in residence card reporting; the online route in immigration procedures online; and if you are choosing the next school now, the questions that actually separate schools.

Statute citations and the agency's own pages are linked below. Individual cases are judged individually, and those pages are the only authority.

claims_without_sources: 「移籍の届出だけ出して離脱の届出を出さない人が多い」—— 実務上よく見る形だが、入管庁は届出の不備の統計を公表していない。頻度を数字で書かず、様式が別立てで併用様式まで用意されている（これは出典あり）という事実から読者に判断させる形にした。
「新しい学校の次の入学期が4月で、今は1月」という例 —— 説明のための仮の設定であり、特定の事例ではない。年を含む数字を出さないよう注意した。
「3か月の空白を意図して作る人はいない」—— 当方の観察であって出典のある主張ではない。
「書面で示せるか否かが『正当な理由』の分かれ目になる」—— 入管庁は正当な理由の認定基準を公表していない。したがって「文書があれば認められる」とは書かず、個別判断である（出典あり）という範囲に留め、用意しておく価値があるという助言の形にした。
入学許可書・医療証明書といった具体的な書類名 —— 入管庁が列挙したものではなく、一般に用意しうる例として挙げた。
「空白期間中に就労すると(6)ではなく(5)に移る」—— 条文の構造からの読みであり、入管庁がこの対比を明示的に書いているわけではない。(5)(6)それぞれの条文内容は出典どおりに引いてある。
中途編入を受け入れるかどうかの学校側の基準 —— 学校ごとに異なり、公表もされていない。判断は学校にあると書くに留めた。
